# The multisite installer script

This page is for developers who change or debug the `sevenx_multisite` install, and for hosts who need to know what a
default install does to a database and to `settings/`. It answers: what `settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php`
runs, when, and in which order. All facts are from the file itself (7692 lines in 6.0.15) and from the kernel's
`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php` and `kernel/classes/ezsiteinstaller.php`.

## The class and when it runs

The file defines `class sevenxMultiSiteInstaller extends eZSiteInstaller`. The kernel's `eZSiteInstaller`
constructor calls `initSettings( $parameters )` and then `initSteps()`, so every `new sevenxMultiSiteInstaller(...)`
works out its settings and its list of post-install steps first. The small wrapper files of the package
(see [What it is made of](what-it-is-made-of.md)) each create one and call one method:

```text
CreateSites (kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php)
  include every <settings-file> of the site package
  eZSitePreInstall()            -> preInstall()
  install the required packages (classes, then content)
  eZSiteINISettings()           -> siteINISettings()
  eZSiteAdminINISettings()      -> adminINISettings()
  eZSiteCommonINISettings()     -> commonINISettings()
  eZSiteRoles()                 -> siteRoles()
  eZSitePreferences()           -> sitePreferences()
  eZSitePostInstall()           -> postInstall() = the 50 steps of initSteps()
  then: exp_adminui in the admin siteaccess, the editor siteaccess, the adminui siteaccess
```

The setup front ends (web wizard, kickstarter, `exp:install`) all run `CreateSites`, so this is the same for every
install method. See [How the setup wizard uses packages](../basics/how-the-setup-wizard-uses-packages.md) and
[How the kickstarter and console use packages](../basics/how-the-kickstarter-and-console-use-packages.md).

## Phase 1: settings the installer works out

`initSettings()` reads the parameters the setup passes and stores what the later steps need:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `template_look_class_id`, `template_look_object_id` | the `template_look` class and its first object |
| `admin_account_id`, `guest_accounts_id`, `anonymous_accounts_id` | from the setup's object remote map |
| `main_site_design` | `media` |
| `extension_list` | 60 extensions, see [Extensions it activates](extensions-it-activates.md) |
| `locales`, `primary_language` | the languages chosen in the setup, the first one primary |
| `fallback_locales` | `eng-US` when it was not chosen, because "the bundled content is in eng-US" |
| `user_siteaccess` | the setup's value, `site` by default (`sevenx_site_user` or empty also become `site`) |
| `admin_siteaccess` | the setup's value, `admin` by default |
| `editor_siteaccess` | `editor` |
| `adminui_siteaccess` | `adminui` when the kernel can make it and `exp_adminui` is installed, else empty |
| `site_title` | the title typed in the setup; when it is empty or only repeats the package summary: "Fit & Healthy" (or "Bold Agency" when the user siteaccess is `bold`) |
| `language_based_siteaccess_list`, `language_siteaccess_map` | one siteaccess name per extra language, see [Siteaccesses and languages](siteaccesses-and-languages.md) |
| `host`, `siteaccess_urls` | the site's address and the addresses of the admin, editor, user and translation siteaccesses |
| `var_dir` | `var/site` |

## Phase 2: the pre-install

`eZSitePreInstall()` creates the installer with `array( 'var_dir' => 'var/site' )` and calls `preInstall()`, before
any package is installed:

1. Records the highest node id and object id of the base data in `$GLOBALS['sevenxBaseMaxNodeID']` and
   `$GLOBALS['sevenxBaseMaxObjectID']`. The post-install fix uses them to tell base data from package content.
2. Adds `tags` (ezkeyword) and `publish_date` (ezdatetime) to the `folder` class.
3. Sets `[FileSettings] VarDir=var/site` for the running process, so images and files land in the site's var
   directory.
4. `activateSiteExtensionSettings()`: adds the `settings/` folder of every extension in `extension_list` to the
   running configuration, so the datatypes and INI files of those extensions are known while the classes and objects
   are imported.
5. Registers the datatype directories `ezstarrating`, `ezgmaplocation`, `exp_enhanced_link`, `eztags` and the
   datatypes `ezsrrating`, `ezgmaplocation`, `ngenhancedlink`, `eztags` in `content.ini [DataTypeSettings]`.
6. When `extension/sevenx_authentication_2fa` exists, adds the "Two-step sign-in" field to the `user` class.
7. `dropExtensionTables()`, then `insertDBFile()` for each extension schema: this is where the layout tables and
   their rows come in. See [Layouts data and the share .dba files](layouts-data-and-share-dba.md).
8. Corrects the language ids of `eng-GB` rows in `eztags_keyword` and `eztags`.

## Phase 3: settings, roles and preferences

While `CreateSites` builds the settings it asks the package for its own. The installer returns lists of INI groups:

| Function | Written to | Files |
|---|---|---|
| `siteINISettings()` | the user siteaccess | `menu.ini`, `override.ini`, `toolbar.ini`, `site.ini`, `image.ini`, `content.ini`, `design.ini`, `browse.ini`, `template.ini`, `contentstructuremenu.ini`, `odf.ini` |
| `adminINISettings()` | the admin siteaccess | `toolbar.ini`, `contentstructuremenu.ini`, `override.ini`, `site.ini`, `content.ini`, `icon.ini`, `viewcache.ini`, `odf.ini`, `ezoe.ini`, `menu.ini` |
| `commonINISettings()` | `settings/override/` | `site.ini`, `content.ini`, `menu.ini`, `viewcache.ini`, `staticcache.ini`, `httpcache.ini`, `override.ini`, `forum.ini`, `ezoe_attributes.ini`, `ezxml.ini`, and `sevenxauthentication2fa.ini` when 2FA is installed |

The `settings/override/site.ini` group is written with `discard_old_values`: what it does not set is gone after the
install. `siteRoles()` and `sitePreferences()` return the roles and the administrator's preferences; see
[Roles and policies](roles-and-policies.md).

## Phase 4: the post-install steps

`postInstall()` runs the step list of `initSteps()` through `executeSteps()`. In order:

| # | Step | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | `dbBegin`, `setVersion` | open a transaction, record the solution version (`solutionVersion()`, built from the class constants `MAJOR_VERSION` and `MINOR_VERSION`) |
| 3 | `postInstallFixContentObjectNameLanguages` | make language ids of names, attributes and masks agree with their locale |
| 4 | `postInstallResolveRelationListIds` | turn relation list items stored by remote id into object ids |
| 5 | `postInstallRekeyStarRatings` | move the seeded rating of the "Test Product" onto the installed object |
| 6 | `postInstallImportNewsletterClasses` | import the `cjw_newsletter` classes and newsletter tree |
| 7-8 | `postInstallAdminSiteaccessINIUpdate`, `postInstallUserSiteaccessINIUpdate` | designs, home node, root node and URLs of `admin` and `site` |
| 9-10 | `createTranslationSiteAccesses`, `createSecondarySiteaccesses` | one siteaccess per extra language; `bold` and `bold_ger` |
| 11-12 | `updateTemplateLookClassAttributes`, `updateTemplateLookObjectAttributes` | twelve extra "look and feel" fields and their values |
| 13-14 | `swapNodes`, `removeContentObject` | the legacy node named `eZ Publish` in older clean data is swapped with "Home" and removed; skipped when absent |
| 15 | `removeClassAttribute` | removes `id` from `template_look` |
| 16-31 | sections, roles, user groups | Restricted section, Anonymous/Editor/Partner/Member policies, Partners group, Members group, role assignments |
| 32 | `updateClassAttributes` | folder attribute names "Summary" and "Display sub items" |
| 33 | `setRSSExport` | the feed "My RSS Feed" at `/rss/feed/my_feed` (not for `_clean` packages) |
| 34 | `dbCommit` | commit |
| 35 | `postInstallFixPackageNodesAndExplayouts` | node placement, layout references, menus, tags, embeds; clears all caches |
| 36 | `postInstallImportAdminLayouts` | the three default admin layouts |
| 37-39 | `postInstallCleanUrlText`, `postInstallRegenerateURLAliases`, `postInstallCreateSitePrefixAliases` | URL aliases of both sites, with their path prefixes |
| 40 | `postInstallClearLinksToContentNotInstalled` | block links to pages the package did not install are switched off |
| 41 | `postInstallPlaceOrphanedPackageObjects` | objects installed without a node get one |
| 42 | `postInstallSetSiteHomeAndPrefix` | `PathPrefix`, `IndexPage`, `DefaultPage` of `site`, `bold`, `bold_ger` and the translations |
| 43 | `postInstallCloseInformationPagesOnPublicSiteaccesses` | the `ezinfo` module off on public siteaccesses |
| 44-45 | `postInstallResyncContentClassNames`, `postInstallRepairClassNameLists` | class name lists |
| 46 | `postInstallCreateAdminUISiteaccess` | `settings/siteaccess/adminui` from the admin siteaccess |
| 47 | `postInstallEnableSearchStatsOnEverySiteaccess` | `LogSearchStats=enabled` |
| 48 | `postInstallWriteMultisiteURLSettings` | `settings/override/ezurlmultisite.ini.append.php` |
| 49-50 | `updateObjectAttributeFromString` (twice) | the site logo from `files/default/image/logo.png`, and the site style `ezwebin_design_blue` |

The details of steps 35 to 41 are on [Post-install fixes](post-install-fixes.md).

## When a step fails

`executeSteps()` stops at the first step that reports an error the installer does not handle; the installer's own
`handleError()` commits the open transaction on an abort. The setup then reports `EZSW-080`: "The post-install of
site package '...' stopped at step N of M (...): the steps after it did not run". That is why the code orders the
steps the way it does: the two cosmetic logo steps run last "because executeSteps aborts the whole chain on the first
step that reports an error", and several kernel steps are overridden (`swapNodes`, `removeContentObject`,
`setSection`, `setRSSExport`) to log a notice and carry on when what they name is not there.

> **Tip**
> After a failed install, the step number in `EZSW-080` tells you where to look in this table. The installer and
> the setup write their notices to the debug output, and some of them to the log file `setup.log` through `eZLog::write()` (for example "no adminui siteaccess").

## The command-line install method

The class also has an `install()` method for use outside `CreateSites`. It writes the user siteaccess, admin
siteaccess and `settings/override` groups itself, then calls `updateRoles()`, `updatePreferences()` and
`postInstall()`. The setup front ends do not use it; they go through the hooks above.
